First login, your profile and signing out

How to sign in (local or directory account), complete two-factor authentication, recover a forgotten password, set your language and other personal preferences, and sign out.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministrator
📍 WhereSign-in page (URL /auth/login) · user menu (top right) → Profile (URL /auth/profile) · Settings → My Account

What is it?#

Every person who uses SATOM signs in with their own account. The account is either local (the password is stored in SATOM) or external (the password is checked by a directory: Active Directory, LDAP or RADIUS). After signing in you land on the Global home and can adjust a few personal preferences on your Profile page.

What does it do?#

  • Signs you in with a username and password, optionally keeping you signed in (Remember me).
  • Asks local accounts that enabled two-factor authentication for a 6-digit code (or a one-time backup code).
  • Lets a local account with a recovery email reset a forgotten password by email.
  • Protects accounts: 10 consecutive failed sign-ins lock the account for 15 minutes, and sign-in attempts are limited to 5 per minute.
  • Stores your personal preferences in the database (not in a browser cookie): language, bookmark grouping order, top-bar banner per product, and — for administrators — whether the Calendar is shown.

Requirements#

  • An account created by an administrator (see Users and profiles), or a directory account when a directory backend is configured in Settings → Authentication.
  • On a fresh installation, the only account is admin. Its password is the one entered during installation. If the guided setup was left to generate one, it is written to a root-only file on the server (/root/satom-admin-password.txt); an installation created without any password writes a random one to the file initial-admin-password in the installation directory.
  • Password reset by email additionally needs email to be configured on the server and a recovery email on your account.

Permissions#

Signing in, the Profile page, the language setting, Two-Factor Authentication and Change Password are available to every signed-in user — no permission is needed.

  • The Calendar switch on the Profile page is only shown to users who can open the Calendar (administrators, users.manage).
  • An administrator may restrict where non-administrators can sign in from (Settings → Access Control, IP allow-list). Administrators and connections from the server itself are never blocked by that list.

How to use#

Sign in#

  1. Open the SATOM address in your browser, for example https://satom.example.com.
  2. Enter your Username and Password. The eye icon shows the password while you type.
  3. Tick Remember me if you want the browser to keep you signed in.
  4. Click Sign In.
  5. If your account uses two-factor authentication, the Two-Factor Authentication page opens: type the 6-digit code from your authenticator app in Authentication code and click Verify. You can type one of your backup codes instead. Cancel and sign out returns to the sign-in page.

After signing in you land on the page you originally asked for, or on the Global home.

❗Important — First sign-in as `admin`

Change the installation password immediately (see Change your password below), delete the generated password file from the server, and create personal accounts for everybody else. Shared use of admin defeats the audit log.

Directory (Active Directory / LDAP / RADIUS) accounts#

Type your directory username and password on the same form. SATOM asks the configured directory to verify them.

  • The first time you sign in, SATOM creates your local account with the default profile chosen by the administrator (readonly unless changed).
  • If the administrator requires approval, your first sign-in creates the account disabled and shows: "Your account was imported from the directory but is still awaiting administrator approval."
  • Directory accounts reset their password and do two-factor at the directory, not in SATOM.
  • A local account never falls through to the directory, even if the directory has a user with the same name.

Forgot your password#

  1. On the sign-in page click Forgot password?.
  2. Enter your Username and click Send reset link.
  3. The page always answers "If that account exists and has a recovery email on file, a password-reset link has been sent." — it never reveals whether the account exists.
  4. Open the link in the email (valid for 1 hour), enter New password and Confirm new password (12 to 1024 characters) and click Set new password.

If the page says "Email is not configured on the server, so reset links cannot be sent. Ask an administrator to reset your password.", ask an administrator.

The link in the email points at the address you used for the sign-in page only when that is one of the node's own names or a name the administrator listed in LINK_HOSTS; otherwise it points at the node's full host name. If the link opens a name you cannot reach (for example you sign in through a public alias), ask the administrator to add that alias to LINK_HOSTS (see Configuration files).

Set up two-factor authentication#

  1. Open Settings (bottom of the sidebar) → My Account → Security.
  2. Under Two-Factor Authentication (TOTP) click Set up 2FA, scan the QR code with your authenticator app and confirm with Enable.
  3. Save the backup codes that are shown. Each works once.
  4. On the same tab, Account Recovery stores the recovery email used by Forgot password?.

Later you can Regenerate backup codes or Disable 2FA from the same card.

Change your password#

  1. Open Settings → My Account → Change Password.
  2. Fill in Current Password, New Password (12 to 1024 characters) and Confirm New Password.
  3. Click Update Password. The page confirms "Password changed successfully."

There is one password rule everywhere: at least 12 and at most 1024 characters, length only (no required character classes). Existing passwords keep working; the rule applies when a password is set or changed.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: every password path (Change Password, the reset link, the administrator's Add User and reset forms, the command-line tool and both installers) applies the same rule of 12 to 1024 characters; before, the web console asked for 8.

Your profile page#

Open the user menu (your initial and username, top right) → Profile. The page My Profile shows your username and role, and these cards:

Card What it changes
Bookmarks — grouping order The nesting order of the device tree in the Bookmarks panel (Level 1, Level 2, …). Click Save order.
Language Your Preferred language. Click Save Language.
Calendar (administrators only) Show the Calendar on or off for your account only. Hiding it does not stop any scheduled change.
Branding — Top-bar Banner Your own top-bar colour per product ADOM. Click Save Banners.
About SATOM The running version and a link to Settings → Change Password.

Choose your language#

  1. User menu → Language (the entry shows your current code, or not set).
  2. Pick a Preferred language and click Save Language.

The interface is offered in English, Español, Deutsch, Français and Italiano, limited to the languages your administrator has enabled. With No preference — ask me each time, the interface follows your browser's language, falling back to English. The language you pick is also pre-selected wherever SATOM asks for a document language (for example change documents).

Sign out#

User menu → Sign Out. You return to the sign-in page. Signing in and out are both recorded in the Audit Log.

Automatic sign-out after inactivity (Session Lock)#

If you do nothing in the console for longer than the Session Lock time an administrator set in Settings → General → Session Lock (minutes) (5–1440, default 60), your next click signs you out and the sign-in page shows "Your session was locked after N minutes of inactivity.". Sign in again and you return to the page you asked for.

  • Only your own actions count as activity: opening pages and submitting forms. Background refreshes — the notification counter, job progress, status badges, edit-lock heartbeats — do not keep the session alive, so a tab left open still locks.
  • API tokens (Bearer) are not affected.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: Session Lock is enforced as an idle timeout; before, the setting was saved but sessions stayed signed in until the browser cookie expired.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Username Your SATOM or directory username. Yes jdoe
Password Your password. Yes —
Remember me Keep the browser signed in after it is closed. No ticked
Authentication code 6-digit TOTP code, or a backup code. Only with 2FA 492817
Preferred language Interface language; empty = follow the browser. No Deutsch (DE)

Result#

  • A successful sign-in starts your session, stamps your last-login time and writes a login entry to the audit log (with the source: local or directory).
  • You are taken to the page you requested or to the Global home.
  • Preference changes take effect on the next page you open.

Troubleshooting#

"Invalid username or password."#

Possible causes - Wrong username or password (passwords are case-sensitive). - A directory account while the directory is unreachable or rejects the bind.

Solution 1. Retype the password using the eye icon to check it. 2. Directory users: confirm you can sign in to another directory-backed system. 3. Use Forgot password? (local accounts with a recovery email) or ask an administrator.

Verification — the next attempt lands on the Global home.

"Too many failed attempts — account temporarily locked. Try again later."#

Possible causes - 10 consecutive failed attempts on this account; it is locked for 15 minutes, whatever address the attempts come from.

Solution 1. Wait 15 minutes, then sign in with the correct password. 2. If you suspect someone else is guessing, tell an administrator — lockouts are logged in the audit log (login.lockout).

Verification — a successful sign-in clears the failure counter.

HTTP 429 "Too Many Requests" when pressing Sign In#

Possible causes - More than 5 sign-in attempts per minute from your address.

Solution — wait one minute and try again. Opening the sign-in page itself is not counted.

"Your account was imported from the directory but is still awaiting administrator approval."#

Possible causes — the directory accepted your password, but new directory accounts need approval.

Solution — ask an administrator to enable your account in Users and profiles.

"This account is disabled."#

Solution — an administrator must re-enable the account.

"Invalid authentication code."#

Possible causes - The code expired while you typed, or the phone's clock is wrong. - A backup code that was already used.

Solution 1. Wait for a new code and enter it promptly; check the phone's time is set automatically. 2. Use an unused backup code. After a backup code works, the page tells you how many are left: "Backup code accepted. N backup code(s) left." 3. Lost the device and all codes: an administrator must reset your 2FA.

"Please log in to access this page."#

Possible causes — you opened a page without being signed in, or your session ended.

Solution — sign in again; you are sent back to the page you asked for.

"Your session was locked after N minutes of inactivity."#

Possible causes — nothing was done in this browser for longer than the Session Lock time (Settings → General). Background refreshes do not count as activity.

Solution — sign in again; you return to the page you asked for. An administrator can change the time in Settings → General → Session Lock (minutes) (5–1440).

"Access denied — You don't have permission to view this page."#

Possible causes - Your profile lacks the permission the page requires. - Your address is not on the administrator's IP allow-list.

Solution — ask an administrator to check your profile or the allow-list. See Permissions.

"That language is not offered on this installation."#

Possible causes — the administrator withdrew that language after your page was loaded.

Solution — reload the Profile page and pick a language from the list. If your saved choice was withdrawn, it is shown as no longer offered here and kept for when it is switched back on.

"Current password is incorrect." / "New passwords do not match."#

Solution — retype the current password exactly, and make sure New Password and Confirm New Password are identical.

Advanced#

Advanced Account protection and sessions
  • Every failed sign-in to a local account writes a login.fail audit entry (directory failures are logged as login.external_fail).
  • Lockout: 10 consecutive failures → locked for 15 minutes (login.lockout audit entry; further attempts while locked are logged as login.locked_attempt). A successful sign-in resets the counter.
  • Rate limits: sign-in POST 5/minute, 2FA page 10/minute, forgot-password 5 per 15 minutes, reset link 10 per 15 minutes (per client address).
  • Password reset links are signed tokens valid for one hour; directory accounts cannot use them.
  • The mailed link keeps the request's host (and port) only when the host is the node's own host name or FQDN, or is listed in LINK_HOSTS. Any other Host header — which anyone can forge on the unauthenticated Forgot password form — is replaced by the node's FQDN, so a forged request cannot mail a live token that points at another server.
  • Idle lock: every page load, Turbo visit and form submission stamps the session with the time of your last activity; script polls are checked against the timeout but do not extend it. A request that arrives after more than Session Lock (minutes) of inactivity signs you out, writes a session.idle_lock audit entry, and redirects to the sign-in page (script callers receive JSON 401). Signing in and out are never blocked by the lock.
  • One password rule — 12 to 1024 characters, length only — is enforced on every path: Settings → Change Password, the reset-link form, the administrator's Add User and password reset, the command-line tool, and both installers (plain and guided). Existing passwords are not re-validated.
